title: The Goldilocks Rule: How to Stay Motivated in Life and Work
coreMove: Keep the challenge at the edge of ability so attention stays alive.
sourcePressure: Motivation stays strongest when the task is just hard enough to demand attention without tipping into discouragement or boredom.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Mistaking calibrated challenge for constant novelty, grind, or maximum difficulty.

hook: starting with a definition of Goldilocks Rule
counterintuition: the problem is not motivation alone

exampleSpecs.domain: a chess coach setting puzzles one rating band above a student
exampleSpecs.audience: a player bored by easy drills and crushed by master games
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether challenge is calibrated enough to hold attention
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the coach swaps a 1900 puzzle for a 1450 puzzle and the student leans in instead of shutting down
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a chess clock beside a puzzle book with a rating tab

exampleSpecs.domain: a rock-climbing setter adjusting a route by one hold color
exampleSpecs.audience: a gym member stuck between boredom and falls
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether difficulty changes by a manageable edge
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the setter removes one green foothold and the climber falls once, then solves it on the third try
exampleSpecs.firstImage: green footholds scattered below a route wall

exampleSpecs.domain: a piano teacher assigning a passage at 86 beats per minute instead of full tempo
exampleSpecs.audience: a student losing motivation from impossible jumps
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether the task stretches without breaking
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the metronome clicks at the edge where mistakes appear but the line still survives
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a metronome blinking beside marked sheet music
mustAvoid: music repetition already used as cue

exampleSpecs.domain: a claims adjuster learning fraud review through borderline files
exampleSpecs.audience: a trainee bored by obvious cases
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the supervisor replaces easy fraud flags with ambiguous files and error notes become specific
exampleSpecs.firstImage: three claim folders labeled borderline on a metal tray

exampleSpecs.domain: a youth fencing coach rotating bouts by skill gap
exampleSpecs.audience: a coach retaining beginners through the hard middle
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether opponents are just difficult enough to teach
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the beginner loses 5-3 instead of 5-0 and asks for one more bout
exampleSpecs.firstImage: foil masks lined along a strip boundary

exampleSpecs.domain: a software learner raising test difficulty only after two clean passes
exampleSpecs.audience: a bootcamp student oscillating between boredom and panic
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether challenge ladder keeps attention alive
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: after two passing tests, she unlocks one failing edge case instead of jumping to a whole new project
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a failing test line highlighted on a laptop screen

skillTargets: adjust difficulty one notch at a time

tryThisNowSpec: Adjust one practice task so it is neither easy nor impossible: add or remove one notch of difficulty before the next rep.
